record.paper_title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let Z be a complemented subspace of a Plichko Banach space X. Must Z be Plichko?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.9. Let Z be a complemented subspace of a Plichko space X. Must Z be Plichko?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $X$ be a (real or complex) Banach space with dual $X^*$. A biorthogonal system $\{(x_\alpha, x_\alpha^*) : \alpha \in \Lambda\} \subset X \times X^*$ is called a Markushevich basis (M-basis) of $X$ if the linear span of $\{x_\alpha\}$ is dense in $X$ and the functionals $\{x_\alpha^*\}$ separate the points of $X$. For a subset $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda$, let
$$X^*_\Gamma := \{x^* \in X^* : \{\alpha \in \Lambda : x^*(x_\alpha) \neq 0\} \subseteq \Gamma \text{ is countable}\}.$$
An M-basis $\{(x_\alpha, x_\alpha^*)\}$ is said to be norming if there exists a constant $\lambda \in (0,1]$ such that the subspace 
$$N := \{x^* \in X^* : \{\alpha \in \Lambda : x^*(x_\alpha) \neq 0\} \text{ is countable}\}$$
is a $\lambda$-norming subspace of $X^*$, meaning $\|x\| \le \lambda^{-1} \sup\{|x^*(x)| : x^* \in N,\ \|x^*\| \le 1\}$ for all $x \in X$. A Banach space $X$ is called Plichko if it admits a norming M-basis.

A closed subspace $Z \subseteq X$ is complemented in $X$ if there exists a bounded linear projection $P : X \to X$ with $P(X) = Z$.

Problem. Suppose $X$ is a Plichko Banach space and $Z \subseteq X$ is a complemented closed subspace. Must $Z$ itself be a Plichko Banach space?

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every complemented subspace of a Plichko Banach space is again Plichko is listed as an open problem in recent surveys on norming Markushevich bases. Web search did not produce any source announcing a solution (positive or negative) to this problem, so it appears to remain open.
